page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose, 7th-generation instance driven by custom AWS Graviton ARM Neoverse-V1 processors. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance provides 8 dedicated physical CPU cores running at 2.6 GHz with single-threaded execution for 8 vCPUs total. It offers 32 GB of RAM (4 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Direct-attached local storage is bundled into the instance via a 474 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25% and an uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 157.33 GB/sec. General compute metrics show middle-tier results, such as a multi-core Geekbench score of 7982, static web serving throughput of 15.88 GB/sec, and 13.58 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. However, performance degrades on specific routines; bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10% to 25% range, and medium-sized LLM prompt processing shows lower throughput relative to high-frequency x86 alternatives.

The m7gd.2xlarge balances general compute resource density with high-speed local NVMe storage, delivering favorable efficiency for IOPS-sensitive applications that do not depend on x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512. Key trade-offs include moderate CPU encryption speeds and reduced performance on heavy decompression tasks. This configuration is well suited for database operations requiring local scratch space, Redis caching layers, software compilation pipelines, and general web application hosting.
